findings.q1: Yes. The key exists with exactly this name and is a bool, both in AOSP and in the fork: CarrierConfig.java:777-778 (ImsEmergency.KEY_PREFIX "imsemergency." at :702), native CarrierConfig.cpp:599-601 and CarrierConfig.h:2021-2032. Its default is false (assets carrier_config.xml:91, the same in ocd). It is not a CarrierConfigManager key. ConfigAgent.getCarrierInternalConfig (:430-441) takes the key list from the asset defaults, so a carrier config value replaces the default. There is exactly one read: MtcPreconditionManager.cpp:1340-1345 (fork :1354-1359). Telephony, the framework and ImsMedia never read it. Fork commit 9134d919a leaves this key and its check unchanged. The fork's other commit, cae6569ce, only touches ImsCallSessionImpl.java.
findings.q2: The only effect is that IsNeedToStartWaitAudioDedicatedBearerTimer (:1300-1348) returns false for an emergency call. OnSdpReceived and OnSdpSent (:325-339) then do not start the WAIT_AUDIO_DEDICATED_BEARER timer (imsvoice.dedicated_bearer_wait_timer_millis_int, default 8000 ms, CarrierConfigManager.java:7410). It is the last check, after IsDefaultBearerAllowed(AUDIO) at :1330, so it matters only when the default bearer is not allowed. It changes no routing, no domain selection, no PDN and no SIP. What it removes is the expiry handling (:767-795). In an early dialog, expiry always calls QosReserveFailed(RELEASE), and OutgoingState::QosReserveFailed (:129-146) sends CANCEL with CODE_LOCAL_CALL_RESOURCE_RESERVATION_FAILED, or with CODE_LOCAL_CALL_CS_RETRY_REQUIRED when IsCsfbAvailable. That is the 8 s trigger for a CS retry. In a confirmed dialog, expiry follows policy_on_audio_qos_deactivation_int, whose default 1 means MAINTAIN (carrier_config.xml:109). The key does NOT make local resources count as reserved. IsLocalResourceReservedByMediaType (:1222) needs the default bearer to be allowed or QoS to be AVAILABLE, and the precondition confirmation UPDATE (OutgoingState::MaySendPreconditionConfirmation :971-1000, via :263-280) needs that. So the stack still waits for the bearer; it only stops timing out. If a dedicated bearer arrives and is reported, QoS goes IDLE to AVAILABLE and setup proceeds as usual; true only removes the 8 s guard. Gap: a Wi-Fi to LTE handover in early state still starts the same timer without checking the key (:455-460).
findings.q3: It is the same timer path. 8 s is the default 8000 ms. "Media bearer loss" is the default text for both bearer loss and bearer not met (carrier_config.xml:185,195). "Cancelled" fits the early-dialog RELEASE path, because a confirmed dialog defaults to MAINTAIN. But what fixed the measured calls was voice_on_default_bearer_supported_bool=true. That key both stops the timer from starting (:1330) and makes local resources count as reserved (:1222), so the confirmation UPDATE goes out. The skip key does only the first. The voicemail calls were still in setup after 8 s, which suggests Vodafone was waiting for that confirmation. With that network behaviour, the skip key alone would have turned an 8 s cancel into a hang. So the stated basis, that ImsStack should not wait for a bearer that never comes, does not describe the key: the key removes the timeout, not the wait. The measurement covered only normal calls at home on LIDL/Vodafone: no emergency call, no roaming, no check of CS retry. The builder's own study (reports/S20 modem and radio interface study.md:143) says the CS-retry outcome was not checked. Also, with the device values (override XML: voice_on_default_bearer=true, and the fork's voice_on_default_bearer_in_roaming_without_qos=true), IsDefaultBearerAllowed returns true at home and while roaming (fork :1120-1141), because this radio never reports audio QoS. The skip key is therefore never reached on this device. The override XML gives roaming as the reason for this key, and fork commit 9134d919a closed that roaming gap.
findings.q4: Yes, in the cases where the key acts, which are calls where the default bearer is not allowed: a carrier or roaming case where the companion values are not served, or where tests later change them. imsemergency.emergency_qos_precondition_supported_bool defaults to true (CarrierConfigManager.java:8350). Google does not override it for vodafone_de or o2_de (1and1_de and 46 other files set it false), and the builder's study lists it as true on the phone. On a network that enforces the precondition, true leaves the 112 call in setup without the confirmation until the emergency no-answer timer runs out (emergency_ringback_timer_millis_int 100000 ms, carrier_config.xml:93; it starts on a reliable 18x because stop_ringback_timer_by_183_with_sdp_body_bool=false, :746, OutgoingState.cpp:571-586). With false, the call is cancelled at 8 s with a CS-retry cause. On a network that does not enforce it, with a PSAP that rings longer than 8 s, true would help, since false cancels in early dialog. Which case applies is untested. Where a dedicated emergency bearer is set up and reported, true costs nothing except the 8 s guard. Google's data sets the key for no carrier: 0 of 624 kodiak textprotos, while 411 of them set other imsemergency.* keys. Without the record the phone serves ImsStack's default false.

notes: The key exists as a bool, default false, and Google sets it nowhere. It has exactly one effect: an emergency call does not start the 8 s dedicated-bearer wait timer. This is the timer that cancelled the measured VoLTE calls. But the basis does not hold as read. (1) The measured fix was voice_on_default_bearer_supported_bool, which also makes local resources count as reserved so the precondition UPDATE goes out. The skip key only removes the timeout: the stack still waits and never confirms. (2) With the device's default-bearer key at home and the fork's roaming key abroad, IsDefaultBearerAllowed returns true before the skip check, so the key does nothing on this device. Its stated reason (roaming) was closed by fork commit 9134d919a. (3) Where it does act (default bearer not allowed, emergency preconditions on by default), true removes the 8 s cancel that OutgoingState turns into a CS-retry cause. On a network that enforces preconditions, a 112 call could then sit in setup until the 100 s emergency no-answer timer. It would help only on a network without preconditions and a PSAP that rings over 8 s. Neither case was measured, and the builder's study says the CS-retry outcome was not checked. Without the record the phone serves ImsStack's false. Emergency calls here still avoid the 8 s release through the default-bearer and roaming keys, and the fast CS fallback stays.
